n: Commanded to leave Ammonihah, Alma and Amulek go to the land of Sidom, where they find the believers who had been driven out and stoned.

f.g: A nearby land that became a refuge for the believers from Ammonihah.

n: The missionaries tell the refugees what happened to their wives and children — and how God delivered them from prison.
Zeezrom lies sick with a burning fever brought on by guilt. Thinking Alma and Amulek had been killed because of him, his conscience tortured him without relief.

f.g: A striking example of how spiritual anguish can affect the body.

n: Hearing they are alive and in Sidom, Zeezrom takes heart and sends for them.

f.w: his heart began to take courage

n: They come at once. Zeezrom, gravely ill and sick at heart over his sins, reaches out his hand and begs them to heal him.
Alma takes his hand and asks the essential question: do you believe in Christ’s power to save?

f.w: Believest thou in the power of Christ unto salvation

n: Zeezrom answers that he believes everything Alma taught — the very teachings he once attacked.
Alma explains that faith in Christ’s redemption can heal him.

f.g: His faith rests on what he has been taught.

n: Alma prays for the Lord’s mercy to heal Zeezrom according to his faith in Christ.
Zeezrom leaps up and walks, astonishing everyone; word spreads throughout Sidom. Healing of body and soul come together.
Alma baptizes Zeezrom, and he immediately begins preaching. The former accuser becomes a missionary.

f.w: he began from that time forth to preach

n: Alma establishes a church in Sidom and appoints priests and teachers to baptize all who want it.
Many people flock from all around Sidom to be baptized.

f.g: A strong response, like the earlier one in Melek.

n: Ammonihah remains hard-hearted, crediting the missionaries’ power to the devil. As followers of Nehor’s teaching, they saw no need to repent.

f.w: ascribing all the power of Alma and Amulek to the devil
did not believe in the repentance of their sins

n: Amulek has given up everything — gold, silver, possessions, friends, even his father and family — for the word of God.
Alma sees the church in Sidom humbled — pride checked, people gathering at their sanctuaries to worship and praying continually for deliverance.

f.g: A strong restraint — here, pride being held in check.

n: Alma takes Amulek home to Zarahemla, cares for him in his trials, and strengthens him in the Lord — a friend who shares the burden of what Amulek has lost.

f.g: Took care of him; ministered to him.

n: So ends the tenth year of the judges (about 82 BC).
